instruction: Navigate to slide 3 and change the font color of the subtitle text to green

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to slide 3 (index 2) and changing the subtitle/body text font color to green (RGB: 0, 255, 0). Slide 3 has subtitle text 'I'm Rain. Welcome to my education presentation. Follow me at @reallygreatsite to learn more.' currently in color 14288F (purple). The evaluator identifies subtitle/body text (not all uppercase title text) and verifies all such text colors match green within tolerance of 20.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: navigating to slide 3 (using slide_index=2 for 0-based indexing) and changing subtitle text color to green
Getter appropriately identifies subtitle text using placeholder types (2=Body, 7=Subtitle) and non-uppercase text heuristic
Metric correctly compares all extracted subtitle colors against target green (0,255,0) with tolerance of 20, appropriate for color matching
Data flow is correct: getter extracts List[RGB tuples] -> metric receives and compares each against expected target_color
Postconfig appropriately saves file with Ctrl+S before verification to ensure changes persist
Complete coverage: all subtitle text colors are verified, not just partial
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter's text identification logic 'if not run.text.isupper() or is_subtitle' could include mixed-case title text. Consider using placeholder_format.type check as primary criterion

Minor: Getter skips text runs without explicit font color (line 54 check). If subtitle text inherits default color and wasn't explicitly set, it won't be verified. Consider handling inherited colors or documenting this assumption
